question: Pilocarpine reduce the intraocular pressure in persons with closed angle glaucoma by:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Pilocarpine" -> "stimulates muscarinic receptors" -> "contracts iris sphincter muscle" -> "opens the angle of the anterior chamber" -> "increases aqueous humor outflow" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Pilocarpine" -> "increases ciliary muscle contraction" -> "facilitates aqueous humor drainage" -> "reduces intraocular pressure" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Pilocarpine" -> "induces miosis" -> "reduces pupillary block" -> "enhances aqueous humor outflow" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Pilocarpine" -> "causes contraction of the iris sphincter" -> "widens the drainage angle" -> "increases aqueous humor outflow" -> 75%
analysis: Pilocarpine is a muscarinic agonist that primarily works by contracting the iris sphincter muscle, which leads to miosis (pupil constriction). This action helps to open the angle between the iris and cornea, facilitating increased aqueous humor outflow and thereby reducing intraocular pressure in closed angle glaucoma. While it does increase aqueous humor outflow, the most direct mechanism by which it reduces intraocular pressure in this context is through the contraction of the iris sphincter muscle.
